transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Occupational health sent me in. They’re saying I’m not eating enough. I guess most days it’s just black coffee, maybe a plain yogurt, or a few bites of chicken at night. A full meal just feels like… like I’m letting my standards slip.
Are you worried about gaining weight if you eat a full meal?
Yes. If the scale is up even half a pound, I feel this jolt, like I’ve lost control. Then I’ll cut back harder the rest of the day, because I really can’t stand the thought of putting weight back on.
Do you think you would be a failure if you gained weight?

Yeah. I mean… maybe “failure” sounds strong, but that’s how it feels. When I look in the mirror, I don’t see what other people say they see. I just zero in on my stomach and my waist, and if I don’t look lean enough, it feels like I’ve let myself down. It can ruin the whole day.
Is your goal to be as thin as possible?

I don’t know if I’d put it as “as thin as possible.” It’s more that when I look in the mirror, I don’t see what everyone else says. I go straight to my stomach and my waist, and if I don’t look lean enough, I feel like I can’t respect myself. It kind of sets the tone for the whole day.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over the past few months?

Yes. My uniform is loose on me now, like it kind of hangs off, and I’ve had to tighten my belt past the old notches. But even when the nurse said my weight was dangerously low, I still thought I could stand to be a little sharper.
Have you had your period in the past few months?
No… I’m male, so I don’t have periods.
Do you engage in any regular physical activity or exercise?
I’m not really sure what counts as regular. I’m on my feet a lot with work, and I do try to stay active, but I don’t have a clear routine I can point to.
Do you fear that gaining weight would change your body shape in a way that you couldn't accept?
Yes. Even a half pound up on the scale hits me hard, like I’ve lost control. Then I’ll spend the day cutting back more, because I really can’t stand the thought of putting weight back on.
Is there a specific weight or body shape that you think would be acceptable to you?

I don’t think there’s a number where I’d just feel okay. I look in the mirror and I don’t really see what other people say they see. I fixate on my stomach and my waist, and if I don’t look lean enough there, it kind of sets the tone for the whole day. It’s like that’s what I judge myself by.
Do you think you would feel better about yourself if you had a more muscular build, even if it meant weighing a bit more?

I don’t know that more muscular would fix it. If the scale went up, I think I’d still have a hard time with that. When I look in the mirror, I focus on my stomach and waist, and if I don’t look lean enough there, it affects how I feel about myself for the rest of the day.
Do you feel like eating a full meal would make you lose control over your body or your life?

Yeah. A full meal feels like I’m letting my standards slip, like I’m giving in. Most days I keep it to black coffee, maybe a plain yogurt, or a few bites of chicken at night. Occupational health says I’m not eating enough, and that’s part of why I’m here.
Do you think your eating habits are related to trying to achieve a certain body shape or appearance?

Yes. It’s tied to how I think I look. I know I’ve said it already, but when I look in the mirror I don’t really see what other people say they see. I go straight to my stomach and waist, and if I don’t look lean enough there, it affects how I feel about myself that day. It’s like I judge whether I can respect myself based on that.
Is your goal to avoid gaining weight or to maintain a specific body shape?

Mostly it’s to avoid gaining weight. I do want a certain shape too, but the number really gets to me. If the scale is up even half a pound, I get this jolt like I’ve lost control, and then I spend the day cutting back harder. I just can’t stand the idea of putting weight back on.
Have you ever eaten a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you couldn't stop?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I ate more than I planned and felt bad about it, but not a huge amount where I couldn’t stop. That’s not really what happens with me.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I don’t make myself throw up after eating. That’s not something I do.
Do you think your perception of your body shape or weight is different from how others see you?

Yes. People tell me I look thin, or that I don’t need to lose anything, but that’s not what I see. When I look in the mirror, my eyes go straight to my stomach and waist. If I don’t look lean enough there, it can ruin how I feel about myself for the whole day.
Do thoughts about your weight or body shape intrude into your mind throughout the day?

Yes. It comes up a lot. I’ll catch myself thinking about my weight or how my waist looks even when I’m trying to focus on something else. If I look in the mirror and my stomach doesn’t look lean enough to me, it can pretty much set the tone for the whole day. It’s hard to respect myself when I see it that way, even if other people say I look fine.
Do you feel like gaining weight would lead to a loss of control over other aspects of your life, beyond just your body shape?

Yeah… it feels that way. If the scale is even up half a pound, I get this jolt, like I’ve lost control somehow. Then I’ll spend the day cutting back harder, because I can’t stand the thought of putting weight back on.
